Single batch, so color plots by condition only; an outlier that separates the groups inflates classifier accuracy, which is why it must be flagged now

Unpaired human cohort, single batch.
steps.question: Do the 120 whole-blood samples (60 case, 60 control) form two coherent groups, are there outlier or mislabeled samples that would bias the classifier, and do the 120 sample columns of counts.csv match the 120 rows of metadata.csv 1:1?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

constraints: n_top_genes = 500 and transform = vst_blind per the grounded settings
Verify 1:1 sample-ID match between counts.csv and metadata.csv (120 of 120); fail loudly on any mismatch
Report the fraction of non-integer count values; state the import state as delivered, no length offset (R-0169)
Record a keep/exclude decision for every sample departing its group (distance from group centroid greater than 2 SD); downstream steps must use this QC-passed list
steps.description: PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes, and the integrity checks (sample-ID alignment, count integrality) that downstream steps depend on.
acceptance_criteria: PCA and distance heatmap colored by condition saved; departing samples flagged with keep/exclude decisions
1:1 ID match confirmed or the mismatch reported
Integrality fraction reported; if non-integer, the documented log-CPM fallback was used for QC plots and downstream steps informed

caveats: The fixed-count alternative (at least 10 counts in at least 60 samples, R-0002) is permitted; filterByExpr is the method of record here
steps.context: Per R-0058, filter with the group before normalization (50+ per group). Filter on the raw delivered counts, no size factors (R-0026). If T1S1 found fractional counts, run filterByExpr on the delivered values with the same group logic and state it.
steps.question: Which of the 12,000 genes carry enough counts in a 60-vs-60 design to be informative, and how many remain for the DE test?

grounding.reason: filterByExpr low count filter (edgeR) per R-0058@99e1

constraints: filter = filterByExpr with the case/control group on QC-passed samples only, per the grounded setting
Do not apply size-factor normalization before the filter (R-0058, R-0026)
Report genes kept (n_in to n_out) where T2S1 and the report can read it
steps.description: filterByExpr with the case/control group on the QC-passed samples, before any normalization; produces the filtered matrix for the DE step.
acceptance_criteria: Filtered count matrix written and the number of retained genes reported
Filter used the case/control group, not an ungrouped threshold

steps.name: Differential expression case vs control (limma-voom)
caveats: State the R-0015 caution: NB models exaggerate false positives at this cohort scale, which is why fixed-effects limma-voom is used; the controls quantify how well the FDR held
Length offset lost (R-0169): a change in isoform use between case and control can show as differential expression; state it
R-0038 (DESeq2 Cook's distance count replacement) does not apply on the voom path
Use the T1S1 QC-passed sample list; excluded samples stay out of the design and are named
steps.context: With 50+ per group the limma-voom fixed-effects path is the method of record (R-0015): in human population cohorts the negative-binomial count models (DESeq2, edgeR-GLM) exaggerate false positives, even on permuted labels. Input: the T1S2 filtered matrix, QC-passed samples. Counts modeled as delivered with no length offset (R-0169); do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input. The DE gene list is descriptive for interpretation and must NOT pre-select features for the T3S1 performance estimate.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between case and control whole blood, and how large are the differences (log2 fold change with 95% CI at BH FDR below 0.05)?

grounding.reason: Population cohort with 50+ per group: limma-voom fixed-effects model per R-0015@65aa; no length input delivered: counts modeled as delivered, no length offset per R-0169@18ab

constraints: import = gene_counts_without_length_offset and missing_input = quantification_directories_or_avg_tx_length_table per the grounded settings
reference_level = explicit: set the condition factor reference to control before the model; do not rely on alphabetical order
contrast_form = factor_numerator_denominator: case (numerator) vs control (denominator); positive log2FC means higher in case
TMM scaling factors (edgeR::calcNormFactors) before voom (R-0057); no pre-normalization beyond the log-CPM that voom models (R-0026)

pvalue_histogram = inspect_before_adjustment; alpha = 0.05; adjustment = BH; filter_results_by = adjusted_pvalue per the grounded settings; select by padj, never by unadjusted p-value or fold change alone (R-0043)

lfc_threshold_policy = test_against_threshold: the question states no minimum effect size, so test the zero null; additionally report the significant count above the named threshold |log2FC| at least 0.585 (1.5-fold)

R-0015 controls: (a) Wilcoxon rank-sum per retained gene, reporting the fraction of voom-significant genes also significant at BH 0.05; (b) one full label-permutation replicate of the voom test reporting how many genes are falsely significant under shuffled labels
steps.description: TMM, voom, fixed-effects linear model (explicit reference control, contrast case vs control), BH at 0.05, p-value histogram diagnostic, plus the R-0015 population-cohort controls: Wilcoxon cross-check and one label-permutation replicate.
acceptance_criteria: Results table with log2FC, 95% CI, p-value, BH padj per retained gene; significant genes at padj below 0.05; significant set sorted by effect size (R-0089)

Wilcoxon agreement fraction and permutation false-positive count reported
Report fields: method, package versions, design formula and contrast, thresholds, n tested, n DE, count above the named fold-change threshold (R-0041)

steps.name: Case-vs-control classifier: glmnet nested CV
caveats: The lasso gene set is unstable across folds: report selection frequency and treat the genes selected in most or all folds as the robust core
Length offset lost (R-0169): a change in isoform use could contribute to the apparent case/control difference the classifier exploits; state it

Within-cohort estimate: same tissue (whole blood), single batch, same quantification pipeline; generalization to a new cohort, batch, or platform is untested - no external validation set in the inputs
Classes balanced 60/60: accuracy reported together with sensitivity/specificity, never alone
steps.context: Inputs: the full 12,000 x 120 delivered counts (no length offset, R-0169), condition from metadata.csv, T1S1 QC-passed sample list. Per R-0155 each prediction must come from a model that never saw that sample, and the gene filter and scaling are fitted inside each training fold because selection on all samples makes the error estimate optimistic. The T2S1 DE list is descriptive only and plays no role in feature selection. The settings score_test, score_adjustment, signature_provenance, marker_source, marker_species_and_tissue concern predefined external signatures; none exists here, so they do not take effect - the signature is the model's own nonzero-coefficient gene set, whose provenance (source, version, gene count) is stated per R-0134.
steps.question: Can a gene expression model classify case from control, and how accurate would it be on a sample it has never seen - the honest new-sample estimate from held-out predictions?

grounding.reason: Penalized logistic classifier with glmnet, nested cross-validation, and a pROC curve per R-0155@08c2 and R-0134@0f16; filter and scaling inside each training fold per doi:10.1073/pnas.102102699

constraints: classifier_model = penalized_logistic_regression; classifier_validation = nested_cross_validation; classifier_performance = roc_auc_with_confidence_interval; preprocessing_scope = filter_and_scaling_inside_each_training_fold per the grounded settings

score_test, score_adjustment, signature_provenance, marker_source, marker_species_and_tissue are conditional on a predefined external signature; none exists here so they do not take effect - signature provenance (source, version, gene count) recorded per R-0134
Outer CV: 10-fold stratified by condition (6 case / 6 control per test fold), 3 repeats with a different recorded seed per repeat; pool the outer predictions across repeats
Inner CV: 5-fold on the training portion only to select the penalty parameter; choose lambda.1se (sparser, more stable signature; lambda.min is the permitted alternative)
Penalty: lasso - glmnet alpha = 1, family = binomial

Inside each outer training fold before fitting: (a) TMM on training-fold samples only (edgeR::calcNormFactors), (b) log2-CPM, (c) low-count gene filter fitted on the training fold, (d) per-gene mean/SD from the training fold used to standardize train and test portions
Report from held-out predictions only: ROC with AUC and 95% CI (DeLong, pROC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity at threshold 0.5, confusion matrix, per-repeat AUC (mean +/- SD)

Stability: per-gene nonzero-coefficient frequency across outer folds; then refit on all QC-passed samples with lambda from 5-fold CV on the full data - in-sample reference only, never the new-sample estimate
Record all CV seeds; never estimate performance on samples that trained the model (R-0155)
steps.description: Lasso logistic classifier (glmnet, binomial) with nested cross-validation on the full 12,000-gene matrix; TMM, filtering, and scaling fitted strictly inside each outer training fold. Outputs: pooled outer-prediction ROC with AUC and 95% CI (DeLong), accuracy/sensitivity/specificity at 0.5, per-repeat AUC stability, the learned signature with selection frequency, and the full-data refit labeled in-sample reference only.
acceptance_criteria: Pooled outer-prediction ROC saved with AUC + 95% CI (DeLong), confusion matrix, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity at 0.5
Per-repeat AUCs reported (mean +/- SD over 3 repeats)
Final gene set (nonzero coefficients of the full-data refit) exported with coefficients, sign, and selection frequency
Headline new-sample answer is the outer-CV accuracy and AUC, labeled within-cohort; no in-sample number presented as new-sample accuracy

steps.name: Final report

plan.title: Whole-blood case-control classifier with nested CV
plan.analytical_narrative: 12,000 Salmon gene-level counts x 120 human whole-blood samples (60 case vs 60 control, unpaired, single batch). Only the gene-level table was delivered (no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table), so the length-correction state is unknown and every step models the counts as delivered with no length offset (R-0169). T1S1 checks sample coherence and data integrity; T1S2 applies filterByExpr with the group; T2S1 characterizes the case-vs-control difference with the population-cohort-appropriate limma-voom fixed-effects model (NB count models exaggerate false positives at 60 per group, R-0015) plus Wilcoxon and label-permutation controls; T3S1 is the core: a lasso logistic classifier with nested CV, all filtering/normalization/scaling inside each training fold, so the outer-CV AUC and accuracy are the honest new-sample estimate; the DE list is descriptive only and never pre-selects features for that estimate; T1S3 writes the report with the reproducibility record.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
penalized logistic regression (glmnet lasso) with nested cross-validation and pROC AUC
reproducibility report with session info, seeds, versions
reproducibility report with effect sizes beside p-values

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If each group holds 50 or more samples, use limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model for the differential expression test. In a population cohort the sample-to-sample variation does not obey the negative binomial model, and DESeq2 and edgeR then report many false positives, even on permuted labels. The linear model on the log counts with precision weights keeps the false discovery rate closer to the nominal level than the count models, but it also exceeds it on some data. The paper recommends the Wilcoxon rank-sum test at a large sample size. State this caution in the report, and give the Wilcoxon test or a permutation check as the control.
